proposal.hypothesis: For the same audience and the same ROI message, a webinar offer produces more pipeline per dollar than a demo offer.

blocks.text: A LinkedIn Demo arm cannot reach the minimum sample within the budget ceiling. Redesigning around the offers LinkedIn can afford to test.

proposal.title: Content Download vs Webinar offer on LinkedIn for Law Firm Enterprise
proposal.hypothesis: On LinkedIn, a content download offer produces opportunities at a lower cost than a webinar offer for the same audience and message.

control.label: Control
control.description: Webinar offer with the ROI message

variant.label: Variant
variant.description: Content download offer with the ROI message

proposal.decision_rule: Read on day 49. If Content Download's cost per opportunity is at least 30% lower than Webinar's, make it the default LinkedIn offer and confirm on pipeline at day 90. If neither arm gets within reach of Meta's cost per opportunity in settled campaigns, recommend moving LinkedIn budget to Google and Meta.

headline.text: Google's budget moved from Webinar to Demo over the last 8 weeks, yet in settled campaigns Google Webinar returns 3.2x the pipeline per dollar of Google Demo. No campaigns are scheduled past Jun 30, so the next launches decide whether that gets corrected.

what_happened.text: Spend fell 53% week over week to $17,013 across 9 campaigns. Almost all of the drop is campaigns ending: the 6 campaigns live through both weeks were flat on spend.
Like for like, CTR slipped from 2.18% to 1.97% and conversions went from 60 to 57. Delivery softened slightly and lead capture held.
Qualified leads, opportunities and pipeline for the week cannot be judged yet. Inside the lag window, qualified leads are only 27% of what their conversions would normally produce.
The program is winding down. 6 campaigns were still live on Jun 30, 0 are scheduled past it, and weekly spend is down 91% from the peak week.
C119 on LinkedIn is running 24% below its own CTR baseline at 60 days old, past the point where LinkedIn creative starts to wear out.

why.text: Offer is the biggest lever. In settled campaigns Webinar returns 1.42x comparable campaigns and Demo 0.46x, and the gap holds on all 3 platforms. Demo still takes 49% of spend.
Google moved the wrong way. Webinar fell from 55% to 5% of Google spend while Demo rose from 42% to 92%. The only test favoring Demo, E013, ran 5 days on a sample of 31 and is rejected.
LinkedIn takes 31% of settled spend and returns 0.06x comparable campaigns. 24 of its 41 settled campaigns produced no opportunities.
Meta buys leads at $10 each but only 30% qualify, against 63% on Google, so its low cost per lead overstates its value.
Region is not a driver. DACH looks weak on raw numbers, but like-for-like indexes run from 0.93x to 1.10x once platform and offer are held constant.

rationale.text: Google Webinar returns 3.2x the pipeline per dollar of Google Demo in settled campaigns, yet Demo is now 92% of Google spend. The only test behind that shift is a rejected false winner, so this is the largest budget decision resting on no valid evidence.

experiments.expected_learning: If Webinar wins, Google's default offer switches back and the budget follows. If Demo holds up under a valid test, the team keeps the current mix with real evidence behind it.

rationale.text: LinkedIn Demo returns $5 of pipeline per dollar and cannot be tested within the budget ceiling, so the affordable question is which other offer LinkedIn should run. experiments.expected_learning: It tells the team which offer gives LinkedIn its best chance before any decision to cut the channel, and it settles a directional result that campaign data disagrees with.

creative_recommendations.text: Make ROI the default message. It returns 1.29x comparable campaigns, is above benchmark in 6 of 6 platform and offer cells, and two trusted tests agree.

Refresh paid-social creative on a schedule. Meta CTR holds for 6 weeks and LinkedIn for 7 before it decays. CR021, the one active creative that has never run, is available as a fresh variant for Law Firm audiences.
Pull back on Customer Proof until it is re-tested. It returns 0.75x comparable campaigns, yet it took 24% of spend in the last 8 weeks.

Keep Security at exploration level. It returns 0.65x comparable campaigns, exists only in Static, and has no valid test behind it. Do not commission new formats until a small test says it is worth it.
Build on product UI rather than stock photography, and use a customer logo wall rather than a quote card for enterprise audiences. Both come from trusted tests.

risks_and_observations.text: The daily and summary tables disagree on outcomes: the daily table carries only 16% of conversions and 3.5% of pipeline. Every efficiency figure here assumes the summary is the reconciled record, which the data owner should confirm.

LinkedIn Demo could not be tested within the budget ceiling. It is 23% of settled spend at $5 of pipeline per dollar, so the team faces a decision without a test: pause it, or approve a larger test budget.

Do not read LinkedIn's numbers as proof the channel has no value. Platform attribution can under-credit channels that influence enterprise deals, which is why the recommendation is to test before cutting.
Three learnings the team may be relying on point the other way in settled campaign data: E003, E004 and E009. None is overturned, but each deserves a confirmation test before it shapes a plan.
Campaign-to-experiment links are unreliable. 42 of 60 linked campaigns point to an experiment on a different platform, so no result in this brief was attributed through those links.
